source.title: Blender References Not Working | How To Set Up References Tutorial
source.creator: 3DTudor

analysis.study_scope: Orthographic reference-image setup, perspective-import failure, multi-view alignment, and external reference board integration.

episodes.problem: Importing a reference image in perspective view aligns it to the arbitrary camera angle rather than world axes.
episodes.observed_fact: Adding a reference image in User Perspective mode creates a tilted image plane, causing misaligned object editing.
episodes.instructor_claim: Importing reference images in perspective mode causes alignment failure across standard views.
episodes.interpretation: Blender aligns newly added reference image planes parallel to the current view orientation.
episodes.reference_evidence: Image imported in perspective view is tilted relative to global coordinates.
episodes.modeling_decision: Delete misaligned reference and switch to Front Orthographic view before re-importing.
episodes.visible_action: Deleted image plane, pressed Numpad 1 to enter Front Orthographic view, and added Reference Image via Shift + A.
episodes.spoken_reason: Pressing Numpad 1 puts the view straight on, ensuring imported reference aligns perfectly.
episodes.topology_surface_effect: Reference plane is locked orthogonal to the world XZ axis.
episodes.failure: Adding reference image in perspective view caused angled viewport alignment.
episodes.correction: Delete image, enter Front Orthographic view (Numpad 1), and re-import reference.
episodes.transferable_principle: Always switch to an orthographic view (Numpad 1, 3, or 7) before importing reference images to align them with global axes.

episodes.problem: Single reference plane does not provide cross-sectional visibility for 3D modeling.
episodes.observed_fact: Presenter duplicates reference plane with Shift + D and rotates it 90 degrees around Z axis.
episodes.instructor_claim: Duplicating and rotating reference plane creates a multi-angle reference box.
episodes.interpretation: Intersecting orthographic reference planes allow multi-view modeling within wireframe display mode.
episodes.reference_evidence: Two perpendicular reference planes visible surrounding the 3D cube mesh.
episodes.modeling_decision: Duplicate front reference plane and rotate 90 degrees on Z-axis to create side reference.
episodes.visible_action: Pressed Shift + D, Enter, R Z 90, then toggled Wireframe mode using Z pie menu.
episodes.spoken_reason: Duplicating and spinning 90 degrees provides multi-side reference visible in wireframe view.
episodes.topology_surface_effect: Perpendicular reference planes created intersecting at world origin.
episodes.transferable_principle: Duplicate orthographic reference planes and rotate along principal axes to establish multi-view spatial alignment.

episodes.problem: Multiple reference planes clutter Blender viewport performance and layout.
episodes.observed_fact: Presenter demonstrates PureRef software set to Always on Top floating over Blender UI.
episodes.instructor_claim: PureRef provides flexible, uncluttered image reference overlays on top of Blender.
episodes.interpretation: External reference overlay tools prevent viewport clutter while maintaining visible image boards.
episodes.reference_evidence: PureRef window displaying multiple images positioned directly over Blender viewport.
episodes.modeling_decision: Use PureRef utility set to 'Always on Top' (Ctrl + Shift + A) alongside Blender.
episodes.visible_action: Organized images in PureRef canvas and enabled Always on Top mode.
episodes.spoken_reason: PureRef keeps reference images accessible on top of screen without cluttering Blender scene.
episodes.topology_surface_effect: No 3D viewport objects added; clean geometric scene maintained.
episodes.transferable_principle: Utilize dedicated floating reference board software set to 'Always on Top' to manage complex reference collections without cluttering 3D viewports.
